data.title: PM Surya Ghar nears 7 million homes as solar rooftop adoption gathers pace
data.description:
The Centre's flagship rooftop solar scheme, PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, is nearing the seven-million-household milestone, with 6.91 million households covered as of November 26, according to the latest data cited by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).
 
The scheme has disbursed ₹37,989 crore in subsidies and added 20.2 gigawatts (GW) of rooftop solar capacity. With 3.09 million households still to be covered, the government has to accelerate installations to meet its March 2027 target.
 
Under the PM Surya Ghar scheme, residential consumers can receive central financial assistance of up to ₹78,000 for rooftop solar systems of up to 3 kilowatts (kW). The programme aims to reduce household electricity bills while expanding India's renewable energy capacity.
 
 

Scheme is on track

 
Launched in February 2024 with an outlay of ₹75,021 crore, Surya Ghar aims to cover 10 million households by March 2027. Officials quoted by the Hindustan Times said the scheme is on track and gaining momentum with the help of a recently launched QR-based tool, meant to simplify installation for users. 
ALSO READ: TVS family feud: What rights do daughters have over family business assets?
 
The tool has recorded 4,57,561 scans in the three months since its launch on August 20. Of these, 98,110 users generated customised solar plans, while 46,369 contacted empanelled vendors, Moneycontrol reported, citing government data released on Thursday.
 
The tool allows households to generate customised rooftop solar plans, including estimates of installation costs, system capacity, payback periods and potential electricity savings.
 
At the Bharat Renewable Energy (BRE) Summit and Expo 2026 in Delhi on November 2, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the scheme was adding nearly 1 lakh new households every six days. He also said it had reduced electricity bills by around 76 per cent.
 

State-wise installation trends

 
The national figures mask significant differences in implementation across states.
 
According to Solentra's state-wise PM Surya Ghar dashboard, based on data from the National Portal for Rooftop Solar, Uttar Pradesh led with around 9.89 lakh installations as of November 27. Gujarat followed with 9.56 lakh and Maharashtra with 9.43 lakh. Together, the three states accounted for nearly half of the installations recorded in the dashboard.
 
Kerala, Madhya Pradesh and Tamil Nadu reported relatively high application-to-installation conversion rates of 77.6 per cent, 75.5 per cent and 82.6 per cent, respectively.
 
Bihar and West Bengal, however, recorded conversion rates of just 17.6 per cent and 15.2 per cent. Delhi's rate stood at 22.1 per cent.
 
The government estimates that installations across 10 million households could generate around 1,000 billion units of renewable electricity over their lifetime and reduce carbon dioxide equivalent emissions by 720 million tonnes over 25 years.

data.title: WhatsApp partners with Jio, Verizon, more to bring travel eSIM data plans
data.description:
WhatsApp is introducing a feature that will allow users to buy and install data eSIMs for international travel without leaving the messaging app. The feature is intended to help travellers access mobile data abroad without having to purchase a local SIM card at an airport or rely on public Wi-Fi.
 
Announcing the feature, WhatsApp said it is working with eSIM providers and telecom operators, including Reliance Jio, Smart Axiata, Smart Communications and Verizon, among others. The company will begin rolling it out in select countries soon, although it has not specified the markets or a launch date.

How will WhatsApp's travel eSIM feature work?

The feature will allow users to discover, purchase and install a travel data eSIM directly through WhatsApp. This is expected to reduce the need to visit a carrier's store or a third-party website to arrange mobile data before travelling abroad. 
 
ALSO READ: WhatsApp rolls out scheduled messages: How to use it and what to know
 Once installed, the travel eSIM will provide data connectivity at the user's destination. Travellers will be able to continue using WhatsApp with their existing phone number, without having to switch their account or register a new number for the messaging service.
 
According to WABetaInfo, the feature will be accessible through the app's Account section, where users will be able to explore data plans for their destination and complete the purchase. The feature is being prepared for both Android and iOS.
 
WhatsApp has not disclosed the available data allowances, plan durations or prices. It has also not detailed how the plans will be priced across different destinations.

WhatsApp partners with Jio and other telecom providers

To support the service, WhatsApp is working with several eSIM providers and telecom operators. The partners named in its announcement include:
  • Reliance Jio
  • Smart Axiata
  • Smart Communications
  • Verizon
  • Other eSIM providers and telecom partners
The availability of plans will depend on the markets and providers supported by WhatsApp. Although Reliance Jio is among the partners, the company has not confirmed whether India will be among the first countries to receive the feature.
 
WhatsApp said the rollout will begin in select countries soon. Users will see the option within the app when the feature becomes available to them.

When will WhatsApp travel eSIM plans be available?

WhatsApp has not announced a specific launch date or a list of countries where the service will initially be offered. The company said it will begin rolling out the feature in select markets soon, with availability indicated directly within the app.
 
WABetaInfo reported that the feature is being prepared for Android and iOS devices. However, WhatsApp's official announcement does not specify supported devices or operating system requirements.
 
The move expands WhatsApp's role beyond messaging and calls by bringing mobile data plan purchases into the app. It also gives the company another way to integrate services from telecom operators and eSIM providers into its platform.

data.title: AI adoption could put 24 million knowledge-worker jobs at risk: JP Morgan
data.description:
Artificial intelligence (AI) could put around 24 million knowledge-worker jobs at risk worldwide over the next five years, as businesses increasingly use the technology to automate tasks currently performed by employees, according to a report by JP Morgan Wealth Management.
 
The estimate is based on an illustrative scenario in which companies use AI to replace a portion of their workforce rather than simply improve productivity. However, the report cautions that the impact may be felt more through reduced hiring and unfilled vacancies than through large-scale layoffs.
 

AI and employment

 
According to the report, the potential displacement represents around 1.3 per cent of the global knowledge workforce every year over five years.
 
 
This estimate assumes that half of enterprise spending on AI goes towards replacing jobs that would otherwise have been filled, while AI costs approximately half as much as the workers it replaces.
 
The impact could be particularly significant if job losses are concentrated in specific occupations or regions, as this could create wider economic and political pressures.
 
The analysis also highlighted the potential scale of disruption in the United States. If two-thirds of the displaced jobs were located there, around 16 million workers could be affected over five years, equivalent to approximately three million annually.
 
This would represent around 2 per cent of US payrolls each year, more than four times the pace of manufacturing job losses during the 2000s. ALSO READ: WhatsApp rolls out scheduled messages: How to use it and what to know 

How AI may reshape work

 
Despite the potential scale of displacement, the report said the more likely outcome would be a transformation of existing jobs rather than their complete elimination.
 
The report noted that every job involves a collection of tasks, and AI currently can automate or support only some of them. This means employees may increasingly work alongside AI tools rather than be replaced entirely.
 
It also pointed out that AI adoption across industries is likely to remain gradual and uneven, limiting the possibility of widespread job displacement in the immediate future.
 

AI adoption still low

 
The report highlighted that AI is still at an early stage of adoption, particularly outside the technology sector.
 
In the United States, around 6 per cent of work hours are currently AI-assisted, even though nearly two-thirds of tasks could theoretically be exposed to the technology.
 
For businesses to realise returns on their AI investments, adoption will need to extend beyond pilot projects and become more widespread across their operations.
 

AI use expands in India

 
The potential impact of AI on employment is also becoming increasingly relevant in India, where businesses are preparing to expand their use of the technology.
 
According to a joint report by KPMG India and the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), 93 per cent of Indian business leaders plan to deploy AI agents to expand workforce capabilities, while 59 per cent are already using them to automate workstreams or business processes.
 
The report also found that 74 per cent of Indian CEOs believe workforce readiness for AI will significantly influence business growth over the next three years. As AI takes over routine activities such as information retrieval, preparing first drafts and routine analysis, employees are expected to focus more on decision-making, interpreting information and evaluating AI-generated outputs.

data.title: 9.25 lakh Indians became OECD citizens in five years, up 40%: Report
data.description:
Around 925,000 Indian citizens acquired the nationality of a member country of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) between 2020 and 2024, a 40 per cent increase from the previous five-year period, according to the OECD's International Migration Outlook 2026, released earlier this month.
 
India remained the largest country of former nationality among people acquiring citizenship in OECD member countries during the period, ahead of Mexico and Syria, whose nationals accounted for 590,248 and 588,219 citizenship acquisitions, respectively.
 
The number of Indians acquiring citizenship rose from 654,821 during 2015-2019 to 925,000 in 2020-2024. Among other major source countries, acquisitions by Syrian nationals surged nearly five-fold, while those by Chinese nationals declined by 11.9 per cent to 342,808.
  
Acquisitions of citizenship in OECD countries by former nationality (2020–24 vs 2015–19):
 
India: 925,737 (up 41.4 per cent from 654,821)
Mexico: 590,248 (down 3.1 per cent from 609,115)
Syria: 588,219 (up 497.4 per cent from 98,463)
Morocco: 507,951 (up 19.6 per cent from 424,538)
Philippines: 503,679 (up 16.2 per cent from 433,602)
China: 342,808 (down 11.9 per cent from 389,316)
 
The OECD has 38 member countries, including the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, Japan and several European nations.
 
Canada accounts for largest share of Indian citizenship acquisitions
 
Country-specific data show that 230,337 Indians acquired citizenship in OECD member countries in 2024, compared with 224,630 in 2023. Canada accounted for the largest share, with 87,320 Indians becoming citizens in 2024, followed by the US (48,820) and Australia (28,969).
 
The trend was similar in 2023, when Canada granted citizenship to 78,487 Indians, followed by the US (52,360) and Australia (40,361).
 
Canada has been a major contributor to the rise in Indian citizenship acquisitions. Around 261,000 Indians became Canadian citizens between 2020 and 2024, a 150 per cent increase from the preceding five-year period. The US, the UK and Australia also recorded high numbers.
 
The figures point to the growing permanence of Indian migration to advanced economies. While migration flows measure the number of people moving to another country, citizenship acquisitions indicate how many immigrants have taken the additional step of becoming nationals of their destination country. 
ALSO READ: US student visa rule struck down: Relief for Indians, but what next?
 
Indian migration to OECD countries slows
 
Despite the rise in citizenship acquisitions, the pace of Indian migration to OECD member countries slowed in 2024. India remained the largest country of origin for new migrants to the bloc, but the number fell 19 per cent to 494,000 in 2024 from 607,000 in 2023.
 
The OECD report also found that around 3 million people acquired the nationality of an OECD member country in 2025. The US accounted for nearly 900,000 new citizens, an increase of 9 per cent over 2024. Germany and Spain recorded around 300,000 each, with increases of 9 per cent and 6 per cent, respectively.
 
Canada ranked fourth, with nearly 300,000 new citizens, following a 22 per cent decline from the previous year.
 
“Migration remains high, and immigrants now account for 16 per cent of employment across the OECD,” OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann said.
 
With ageing populations and slower productivity growth, countries cannot afford to waste the skills migrants bring, he said, calling for better access to jobs, finance, business networks and support for immigrant entrepreneurs.
 
Immigrants accounted for 12 per cent of the population across OECD member countries in 2025, compared with 9 per cent in 2015. In more than half of the member countries, immigrants contributed at least 50 per cent of employment growth between 2014 and 2024.
 
Leading OECD countries granting citizenship to Indians:
 
2024:
 
Canada: 87,320
United States: 48,820
Australia: 28,969
United Kingdom: 24,888
New Zealand: 5,778
Total across OECD countries: 230,337
 
2023:
 
Canada: 78,487
United States: 52,360
Australia: 40,361
United Kingdom: 18,319
New Zealand: 6,609
Total across OECD countries: 224,630
 
Indian students remain among largest groups overseas 
ALSO READ: Canada could admit 662k permanent residents in 2027, 74% above target: RBC
 
India also continued to be a major source of international students in OECD countries, although overall student inflows declined. The number of international students entering OECD member countries fell from 1.9 million in 2024 to 1.6 million in 2025, with much of the decline concentrated in traditional English-speaking destinations.
 
European countries, particularly Austria, Germany and Italy, continued to attract more international students. China and India remained the two largest source countries. The gap between them narrowed, with 829,000 Indian students and 850,000 Chinese students enrolled across OECD member countries.
 
The report also found that one in five STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) graduates across OECD countries was foreign-born. Immigrants were also over-represented among researchers and founders of innovative businesses. However, many continued to work in lower-productivity firms and sectors, with their skills not being fully utilised.
 
Permanent migration to OECD member countries declined by 1.6 per cent in 2025, falling for the second consecutive year. However, it remained historically high at nearly 6 million new permanent immigrants. The category covers people moving for family reunification, employment or humanitarian reasons with long-term rights to stay.
 
With countries such as the US, the UK, Canada and Australia tightening immigration policies, the decline in temporary worker and student arrivals could continue over the coming years. However, the latest citizenship figures show that Indians continue to account for the largest number of new citizens across OECD member countries.
 
Annual number of Indians acquiring citizenship in OECD member countries:
 
2010: 133,280
2011: 113,640
2012: 105,067
2013: 134,364
2014: 129,190
2015: 127,374
2016: 129,323
2017: 121,151
2018: 121,299
2019: 155,674
2020: 132,621
2021: 132,877
2022: 205,272
2023: 224,630
2024: 230,337

data.title: Waaree Renewable share price rallies 14% after securing 120-MWp EPC order
data.description:
Waaree Renewable Technologies shares defied the market weakness to surge nearly 14 per cent in intraday trade on Friday after the company received a Letter of Award (LOA) for a turnkey project.
 
The stock opened higher at ₹697 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and extended its gains to hit a high of ₹781.50.
 
The rally marked the second straight session of gains for the stock following a nine-day losing streak. During these two sessions, the counter has surged as much as 15 per cent.
 
Today's rally also helped Waaree Renewable Technologies recoup its losses over the past month. According to NSE data, the stock has gained 12 per cent during the period. However, on a Y-T-D basis, the stock has significantly underperformed the market, declining 22 per cent compared with a 1.35 per cent fall in the Nifty.
 
 
As of 10:20 AM, Waaree Renewable Technologies shares were trading 9.6 per cent higher at ₹755.50, with more than 6 million shares changing hands. This made the stock one of the most actively traded equities on the NSE by volume.
 
Waaree Renewable wins order 
 
According to an exchange filing, Waaree Renewable Technologies has received a Letter of Award (LOA) for a turnkey project comprising the supply of modules and execution of Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) works for a total capacity of 120 MWp. 
 
The order was received by a domestic entity and is scheduled to be completed during the financial year 2027-28.
 
The company did not disclose the name of the entity and the value of the project.
 
Waaree Renewable stock: Technical view
 
Sudeep Shah, head - Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities, said that Waaree Renewable Technologies has formed a sizeable bullish candle today, supported by a sharp rise in volumes. However, the stock witnessed profit booking around the ₹775–785 zone, which has acted as a strong resistance in early November. Despite the strong upmove, it would be premature to consider this a trend reversal, as the broader price structure remains largely unchanged.
 
On the weekly chart, the stock continues to trade below key moving averages, keeping the overall bias bearish. The immediate resistance is placed in the ₹775–785 zone, and a decisive, sustained breakout above ₹785 could lead to an extension of the pullback in the near term. On the downside, the 695–685 zone is likely to act as immediate support.

data.title: India-US trade deal: Why talks are back on table amid fresh tariff threat
data.description:
India and the US finalised the framework for the first phase of their bilateral trade agreement (BTA) in February this year, following negotiations that were launched in February 2025.

But changes in Washington's tariff structure have brought the two sides back to the negotiating table.

The US has proposed a fresh set of tariffs on 14 economies, including India. Here is an explainer to understand the developments so far.

WHY THIS TRADE PACT?

India is pursuing the agreement to safeguard the competitiveness of its exports amid high American tariffs and secure an edge over rival South and South East Asian manufacturing economies.

WHY THESE TARIFFS?

The US is using tariffs against its trading partners such as India to address trade deficits, shield domestic industries from foreign competition and press countries to negotiate trade agreements on terms favourable to Washington.

 

The US has alleged that trading partners like India and China impose steep import duties and restrictive regulations on American goods while enjoying low-tariff access to the US market.

WHAT IS A TARIFF?

It is a customs or import duty imposed by the importing country on goods entering its territory and paid by the importer. Tariffs increase the cost of imported goods and can make them more expensive than domestically produced products. They are used to protect domestic industries, generate government revenue and influence trade flows.

WHY US MARKET IMPORTANT FOR INDIA?

The US has been India's largest trading partner since 2021-22. Exports grew 0.92 pc to USD 87.3 billion during 2025-26, while imports increased 15.95 per cent to USD 52.9 billion. India's trade surplus with the US declined to USD 34.4 billion in 2025-26 from USD 40.89 billion in 2024-25.

The US is India's largest export destination for sectors such as textiles, pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, gems and jewellery, chemicals and electronics.

Any increase in tariffs could affect the price competitiveness of Indian products and exporters' ability to retain or expand their market share.

WHY TARIFF LANDSCAPE IN US CHANGING?

The US announced a 25 pc duty from August 7, 2025. An additional 25 pc tariff was imposed on Indian goods as a penalty for New Delhi's continued purchase of Russian oil. After this order, the total tariff on Indian goods, barring an exemption list, rose to 50 pc.

On February 2, 2026, India and the US agreed on a trade deal, under which Washington agreed to bring down the reciprocal tariff on Indian goods to 18 pc. On February 20, the US Supreme Court struck down the reciprocal tariff system.

The Donald Trump administration subsequently turned to Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the US to impose tariffs following investigations into alleged unfair trade practices. The probes into forced labour and excess manufacturing capacity are part of Washington's efforts to rebuild its tariff regime under an alternative legal provision.

On July 24, the US imposed a 10 and 12.5 pc tariff on 60 countries, including India (10 pc), under Section 301, citing concerns related to 'forced labour'.

WHAT TRIGGERED THE LATEST DEVELOPMENTS?

The US Trade Representative (USTR) on November 25 announced the findings of its second Sec 301 investigations into structural excess manufacturing capacity in 14 economies, including India, and proposed additional tariffs on their goods.

For India, it proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent, while indicating that the rate could be adjusted to 17 per cent if the two countries reach a trade agreement.

US ALLEGATIONS ON INDIA?

The USTR has alleged that India's industrial policies (such as the 'Make in India' initiative and PLI schemes), manufacturing expansion plans, labour protections, financial practices and market access barriers contribute to structural excess capacity and hurt American firms.

The report has identified sectors such as steel, solar, pharmaceuticals, medical devices and information and communications technology as areas of concern.

INDIA'S RESPONSE?

India has rejected the allegations, stating that it does not have structural excess capacity in any sector.

It emphasised that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of the trade pact negotiations.

It said India remains committed to working closely with the US towards the early conclusion of the India-US BTA in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026.

JOINT STATEMENT?

The two countries announced that they have reached a framework for an interim agreement regarding reciprocal and mutually beneficial trade. The terms of that pact include: - India will eliminate or reduce tariffs on all US industrial goods and a wide range of food and agri products.

- The US will apply a reciprocal tariff rate of 18 pc on Indian goods, subject to the successful conclusion of the interim agreement.

- Both will address non-tariff barriers that affect bilateral trade.

IMPORTANT: "In the event of any changes to the agreed-upon tariffs of either country, the US and India agree that the other country may modify its commitments." - India intends to purchase USD 500 billion of US energy products, aircraft and aircraft parts, precious metals, technology products, and coking coal over the next 5 years.

CURRENT STATUS OF TALKS?

India has stated on multiple occasions that the deal has been finalised and will be signed once the US tariff framework is in place and India gets a comparative advantage over its competitor nations.

Comparative advantage means securing lower US import tariffs and better market access than rival manufacturing countries, such as Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, and China, so Indian exporters can price goods more competitively in the US market.

HAS INDIA RECEIVED THIS ADVANTAGE?

The latest USTR's report has proposed a 17 per cent tariff on India if the trade pact is finalised. It gives only one per cent edge over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand (18 per cent deal rate) and a 3 per cent edge over Vietnam and China (20 per cent deal rate). Without a pact, tariffs against India could go up to 25 pc.

However, according to experts, Indian exporters could face a tariff disadvantage against goods from several other countries in the US market, as Washington's latest Section 301 investigation into structural excess capacity covers only 14 trading partners, while the probe into forced-labour-related trade practices covers 60 countries.

This leaves a much larger group of economies (including Pakistan, Sri Lanka, the Philippines and Turkiye) potentially outside the additional tariff action, giving their exporters a relative cost advantage in the US market.

EXPERTS VIEW

While exporters are urging the government to finalise the pact at the earliest, think tank GTRI said that with the threat of up to 100 pc Graham tariffs still looming, New Delhi must reject a one-sided trade deal and defend its industrial expansion sector by sector as serving legitimate domestic, export, and future demand.

WHAT NEXT

The USTR has decided to schedule public hearings on its proposals on January 25 and has sought written comments from interested persons by January 5 as part of the final regulatory requirements before the tariffs come into effect.

data.title: WhiteOak Capital raises equity exposure to 65%: What it mean for investors
data.description:
WhiteOak Capital Balanced Advantage Fund on Friday said it has increased its net unhedged equity allocation to 64.9% as of October 31, 2026, signalling a more favourable assessment of equity market valuations by the fund’s internal model.
 
The move comes as the market has corrected from its levels at the beginning of the year. But what does a higher equity allocation in a balanced advantage fund mean, how does the valuation-based strategy work, and should investors read it as a signal to invest more in equities?
 
What has changed in WhiteOak’s allocation?
According to the fund house’s update, its proprietary Market Valuation Index declined from 101 in January 2026 to 90 in October. The BSE Sensex, meanwhile, fell from 82,269 to 74,459 over the same period.
 
 
WhiteOak said its model responds to lower valuations by gradually increasing equity exposure. Accordingly, the fund raised its net equity allocation from 61% in January to 64.9% in October.
 
The fund’s positioning has also changed sharply compared with an earlier period of elevated valuations. In September 2024, when the Sensex reached 84,299 and WhiteOak’s valuation index touched 105, the fund maintained a more conservative net equity allocation of 49.6%. WhiteOak Capital Balanced Advantage Fund Raises Net Equity Allocation to 64.9% as Market Valuations Turn Increasingly Attractive.docx
 
What is a balanced advantage fund?
A balanced advantage fund, also known as a dynamic asset allocation fund, is a hybrid mutual fund that invests in both equity and debt. Unlike funds that maintain a relatively fixed allocation, these schemes can increase or reduce their equity and debt exposure based on market conditions and the fund’s investment model. 
 
The idea is to adjust the portfolio across market cycles:
  • When equity valuations appear expensive, the fund may reduce unhedged equity exposure and move more towards debt or hedged positions.
  • When valuations become more attractive, it may increase equity exposure to participate in a potential market recovery.
  • The allocation can change over time, so the fund’s risk profile is not constant.
SEBI’s investor education material describes dynamic asset allocation funds as schemes that can move between equity and debt within a broad range, subject to their investment mandate. 
 
What does “net unhedged equity” mean?
The 64.9% figure refers to the fund’s net unhedged equity exposure — the portion of the portfolio exposed to equity market movements after accounting for hedges.
 
It should not automatically be read as the fund holding exactly 64.9% of its total assets in shares. Balanced advantage funds may also use derivatives to hedge part of their equity exposure. The gross equity allocation, hedged exposure and net equity exposure can therefore be different measures. 
 
For investors, net unhedged equity is an important indicator of how much market risk the fund is taking through its equity positioning at a particular point in time.
 
Does a higher equity allocation mean the market is cheap?
Not necessarily. It means WhiteOak’s internal model currently considers equity valuations more attractive than they were earlier in the year.
 
The fund house’s Market Valuation Index is proprietary, and the release does not provide its full methodology or the precise valuation threshold at which the fund changes its allocation. The index level of 90 should therefore not be treated as a universal measure of whether Indian equities are cheap or expensive.
 
A valuation-based strategy also does not guarantee that a fund will increase equity exposure at the market bottom or reduce it before a correction. Markets can remain expensive or fall further even after valuations have moderated.
 
What should investors make of this?
The increase in equity allocation is a portfolio-positioning update, not a standalone recommendation to invest in the fund.
Balanced advantage funds may be relevant to investors who want a fund to manage the equity-debt mix dynamically rather than make every allocation decision themselves. However, these funds remain market-linked and can incur losses, particularly when their equity exposure is high. 
 
Investors should look beyond the latest allocation and assess the fund’s longer-term performance across market cycles, its investment strategy, expenses, risk level and consistency of execution. They should also consider whether the fund fits their investment horizon and overall asset allocation.
 
Mutual fund investments are subject to market risks. Read all scheme-related documents carefully.

data.title: Coal India unit Mahanadi Coalfields lists at 2% discount to IPO price
data.description:
Mahanadi Coalfields IPO listing: Shares of Mahanadi Coalfields made a tepid debut on Dalal Street as they listed at a discount of nearly 2 per cent premium against the initial public offer (IPO) price of ₹136. 
 
The Coal India subsidiary made its NSE debut at ₹134 apiece, down 1.47 per cent. And on BSE, the stock listed 2.10 per cent lower at ₹133.15. 
 
Mahanadi Coalfields is the third Coal India subsidiary to make its debut on the bourses, following Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL) in January 2026 and Central Mine Planning & Design Institute (CMPDIL) in March 2026.
 

Mahanadi Coalfields IPO details

The ₹8,981-crore IPO of Mahanadi Coalfields was available for bidding from November 19 to November 23. The offer received a tepid response as it was booked just 1.52 times at the end of the final day. Overall, it received bids for 74,86,87,390 shares as against 49,30,68,045 shares on offer.  
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex down 200 pts, Nifty around 25,800; SMIDs outperform
 
 
The qualified institutional buyers (QIB) did the heavy lifting as their quota was the only one that sailed through. It was subscribed 4.95 times. Meanwhile, the non-institutional investor (NII) portion was booked just 0.66 times, the retail portion 0.46 times, employee portion at 0.22 times, and the shareholder quota at 0.56 times. 
 
The issue was entirely an offer for sale by promoter Coal India, meaning no proceeds would go to the company. 
 
The price band for Mahanadi Coalfields IPO was set at ₹129 to ₹136 per share. Investors could apply for the offer in lots of 110 shares. The minimum amount of investment required by an individual investor was ₹14,960 based on upper price.
 
Mahanadi Coal is India’s largest single coal producing company by production, engaged in the production of thermal-grade non-coking coal. It also ranks amongst the country’s largest coal resource holders, holding ~9.8 per cent of India’s total coal resource. 
 
Financially, the company has maintained strong profitability despite moderating revenue and earnings. Consolidated revenue from operations declined from INR 31,634.35 crore in FY24 to INR 31,353.02 crore in FY25 and INR 30,549.59 crore in FY26, representing a 1.73% decline CAGR over FY24–26. Consolidated PAT decreased from INR 11,841.55 crores in FY24 to INR 10,825.12 crores in FY25 and INR 10,698.12 crores in FY26.  
ALSO READ: PhonePe warms up for IPO as investor appetite for Indian equities returns
 
Operating cash flow improved to INR 12,477.53 crores in FY26 from INR 7,704.96 crores in FY25, reflecting strong cash generation despite subdued earnings growth. The balance sheet remains highly liquid, with minimal financial borrowings and substantial cash and bank balances, said Ventura. 
 
Key risks, according to the brokerage, include thermal coal demand dependence, pricing and regulatory changes, rising mining costs, environmental obligations and the long-term transition towards renewable energy.
 
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: India Inc margins may fall 50-75 bps, revenue growth at 18-20% in Q3: Icra
data.description:
Rating agency Icra expects revenue growth of Indian companies to moderate to 18-20 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in Q3 FY27, from 24.2 per cent in the previous quarter, as rising input costs and price increases are likely to weigh on volume growth.
 
However, price increases, festive and wedding-season spending, and sustained government capital expenditure are expected to support revenues, even as operating profit margins (OPM) face pressure.
 
In its latest assessment of 3,103 listed companies, excluding those in the financial sector, Icra estimated that aggregate operating margins could decline by 50-75 basis points year-on-year in Q3 FY27, amid higher raw material, fuel, freight and packaging costs.
 
 
The rating agency said the moderation in revenue growth would partly be due to a high base in Q3 FY26, when volumes received a boost following the goods and services tax (GST) rate cuts in September 2025. Companies are also passing on higher raw material, energy, labour and logistics costs to customers through price increases.
 
Icra said inflationary pressures and a possible slowdown in rural demand following El Niño-related crop losses could pose challenges over the next two to three quarters. An uneven monsoon could also weigh on agricultural output, farm incomes and rural consumption.
 
"Icra expects the divergence between domestic-oriented and export-oriented sectors to persist in the near term," said Kinjal Shah, senior vice-president and co-group head, Corporate Ratings, Icra.
 
Sectors such as automobiles, retail, consumer durables and hospitality are likely to perform better, supported by relatively resilient domestic demand. In contrast, export-dependent industries such as information technology and cut and polished diamonds could continue to face challenges amid subdued global demand and macroeconomic uncertainty.
 
A softening of US tariffs could provide some support to apparel and home textile exports, although any fresh tariff-related uncertainty remains a concern, Icra said.
 
On the profitability front, aviation, automobiles, fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), cement and other energy-intensive industries are likely to face margin pressure from higher crude oil prices, palm oil, coal and other key inputs. The resulting increase in freight, packaging and logistics costs is also expected to weigh on profitability.
 
Companies in these sectors have started taking price increases and cost-cutting measures to offset higher expenses arising from the West Asia conflict and the depreciation of the rupee against the US dollar. However, the benefits are expected to come through gradually.
 
Metals and mining companies, upstream oil producers, telecom operators, hospitality players and regulated utilities are relatively better placed, supported by favourable realisations, operating leverage and established mechanisms to pass on higher costs.
 
Despite the expected pressure on margins, corporate credit metrics are likely to remain resilient. Icra expects the interest coverage ratio of its sample companies to stand at 5-5.2 times in Q3 FY27, compared with 5.7 times in Q2 FY27.
 
The ratio is expected to be supported by stable earnings and healthy revenue growth, although higher borrowing costs and lower margins could weigh on it.
 
Icra also cautioned that inflation, product price increases and interest rate hikes could affect consumption, particularly in mass-market and price-sensitive categories. Geopolitical developments, commodity price movements and climate-related risks are also likely to influence business sentiment and private sector capital expenditure plans in the coming quarters.

data.title: India-US trade deal close to completion: Goyal amid fresh tariff threat
data.description:
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Friday said the India-US trade deal is nearing completion, with the process and roadmap for finalising the pact, which had earlier held up negotiations, now taking shape.

"The US trade deal is close to culmination. The process and pathway, which was always something which held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape," Goyal said while addressing the India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026 virtually.

The remarks came after the latest US Trade Representative's (USTR) report proposed 25 per cent tariffs on imports from India, with a provision to cap them at 17 per cent if the two countries agree to a bilateral trade deal, giving it a slight edge over Asian competitors.
